A former Governor of Abia State and presently the Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu has defended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s reform initiatives, predicting that the President will, come 2027 presidential election, have a landslide victory. Kalu spoke during an appearance on Arise PrimeTime, the flagship evening current affairs programme of Arise News Television, where he defended Tinubu’s economic reforms, stating “Nigeria’s economy has stabilised”. The former Senate Chief Whip, who currently chairs the Senate Committee on the South East Development Commission (SEDC), on Monday defended the Tinubu administration against criticism over the economic hardship associated with its reforms, and argued that “the President has successfully stabilised Nigeria’s economy at the macroeconomic level, although more work remained to improve conditions at the household and business levels”. According to him, the immediate challenge before the administration is translating macroeconomic stability into tangible economic growth, increased manufacturing capacity, employment opportunities and improved living conditions. “President Tinubu has been able to stabilise this economy on the macro level. What we are battling now, have stabilised economy on the macro level. What we are battling is the micro level,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He explained that the administration’s next priority should be restoring agricultural production, improving security and creating an environment in which manufacturers can access raw materials and operate at higher production capacity. Acknowledging the difficulties confronting ordinary Nigerians, Kalu, insisted that the country was beginning to experience greater economic predictability, maintaining that economic reforms inevitably come with temporary difficulties. Kalu further credited Tinubu with improving Nigeria’s international economic relationships, arguing that the country was increasingly attracting the attention of international investors. President Tinubu have no competition. The APC’s electoral strength goes beyond the personality of the President. The ruling party enjoys a broad political structure and substantial grassroots support across the country. “What we are seeing as social media, we are not seeing something on ground. Our party is very huge and supporters of that party are large and we have huge people supporting this party,” he said. He added that APC legislators and other political stakeholders were already working towards consolidating the party’s electoral strength in their respective constituencies to ensure Tinubu’s re-election and made a passionate appeal for political stability. “The unity of this country is very important. Let’s not question the unity. We allowed President Buhari to do his eight years and go, and we must allow Tinubu to do his eight years and go,” he said. He urged Nigerians to assess the administration’s economic policies against the long-term objective of rebuilding the economy rather than the immediate discomfort associated with the reforms.
